title: Project context: A fungicide yield response is not automatically profitable
text: Wise et al. (2019) analysed hybrid corn trials conducted in 2014-2015 in the United States and Ontario, Canada. Their yield-response estimates and between-study variation were used to estimate the probability of recovering fungicide product and application costs across historical corn price-cost combinations. A positive average yield response does not guarantee a profitable application. Keep response uncertainty, grain value and treatment costs separate. These study estimates are historical research context; they supply no current prices, product permission, field efficacy forecast or universal disease threshold. Any field decision still requires current local label, scouting, cultivar susceptibility, growth stage and farm-specific costs. Source basis: doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0217510; this project paraphrase excludes numerical treatment effects and product recommendations.
application_boundary: Ontario-scoped candidate context only. The study does not authorize a product or a preventive application in another crop. Obtain current local label, scouting, cultivar susceptibility and crop-stage evidence; keep historical prices dated.
applicability_boundary: Ontario-scoped candidate context only. The study does not authorize a product or a preventive application in another crop. Obtain current local label, scouting, cultivar susceptibility and crop-stage evidence; keep historical prices dated.

title: Project context: Daymet V4 gridded weather is an estimate with application-specific error
text: Thornton et al. (2021) describe Daymet V4 daily weather estimates on a one-kilometre grid for North America. For primary temperature and precipitation variables, cross-validation withheld a variable-station-year record and compared estimates with available daily observations. Its station-level paired estimates and observations help assess suitability for a region, period and variable; error varies with station density, terrain and time. A grid cell is an estimate rather than a field rain gauge or a seasonal forecast. Retain the dataset version, dates, calendar convention, variables, units and missing-data flags, and assess local error before a water-balance decision. This describes the V4 release in the 2021 paper and establishes no current dataset version, current weather observation or field calibration. Source basis: doi:10.1038/s41597-021-00973-0; project-authored paraphrase only.
application_boundary: A grid cell is not a field rain gauge or a seasonal forecast. Retain dataset version, dates, calendar convention, variable and units; assess local error before a water-balance decision.
